title: CPD vs CPE vs CLE: what is the difference between continuing education terms?
description: CPD, CPE and CLE all mean ongoing learning required to keep a professional credential. How terms, units, cycles and evidence rules differ by profession.
shortAnswer: CPD (continuing professional development), CPE (continuing professional education) and CLE (continuing legal education) all describe ongoing learning a professional must complete to keep a license, registration or membership. The difference is mostly who uses which term: CPD is common in Australia and the EU; CPE is the US accounting term, also used by Australia's Tax Practitioners Board; CLE is the US term for lawyers. Units, cycles and evidence rules are set by each regulator or professional body.
keyTakeaways: The terms overlap in meaning; the practical differences are the unit of measure, the cycle length, mandatory subject areas and the evidence the body accepts.
CPE for US CPAs is measured in credits of 50 minutes under the AICPA and NASBA Statement on Standards for CPE Programs, revised with an August 1, 2026 effective date.
CLE is set state by state; California, for example, requires 25 hours in each three year compliance period with specified ethics, bias, competence, technology and civility hours.

CPD in Australia may be a statutory condition (health practitioners, lawyers) or a membership by-law (CPA Australia); in the EU, the Insurance Distribution Directive sets at least 15 hours a year for insurance distributors.
Employers rarely own these obligations but usually supply much of the learning, so course records should carry the fields each body needs.

sections.heading: What is the difference between CPD, CPE and CLE?

blocks.text: The three terms name the same idea, structured ongoing learning required to maintain a professional credential, but each is attached to particular professions and regulators. Which one applies depends on the credential held, not the content of the learning.

The [Statement on Standards for CPE Programs](https://cdn.asp.events/CLIENT_NASBA_287596D2_5056_B733_49DFF69B632BDF66/sites/nasba-registry-composer-2/media/Documents/2026-Statement-on-Standards-for-CPE-Programs.pdf), jointly issued by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) and the National Association of State Boards of Accountancy (NASBA), defines CPE as "an integral part of the lifelong learning required to provide competent service to the public" and "the set of activities that enables CPAs and other professionals to maintain or improve their professional competence." CPD and CLE carry the same intent in their professions.

items: **CPD** is used by Australia's health practitioner boards, CPA Australia, Australian law societies, and EU instruments such as the Insurance Distribution Directive.
**CPE** is used for US certified public accountants and by Australia's Tax Practitioners Board for registered tax and BAS agents.
**CLE** is used by US state bars and courts for attorneys, often as MCLE (minimum or mandatory continuing legal education).

blocks.text: Two patterns stand out. First, the unit varies: hours, units, points and 50 minute credits are not interchangeable without checking each body's rules. Second, most bodies now require minimum hours in ethics or professional responsibility, and some add topics such as bias, technology or civility.

sections.heading: How are credits measured and evidenced?

blocks.text: Each body defines what counts, how much it counts for and what records must be kept. Getting these wrong is the most common reason learning fails to count.

items: **Unit length:** under the AICPA and NASBA standards, "Fifty minutes of participation in a formal learning program equals one CPE credit." Many CPD and CLE schemes use 60 minute hours or units instead.

**Activity caps:** many bodies cap passive or self directed learning; NSW solicitors, for example, may count no more than 5 units of private audio or visual study, and the TPB limits technical reading to 25% of CPE.
**Verifiability:** CPA Australia states that slides, registration emails or course materials are not sufficient verification for ethics CPD.
**Record retention:** periods differ, for example at least five years for NMBA CPD records, five years from the end of the period for TPB CPE, and at least three years for NSW solicitors.
**Audit:** most bodies audit a sample after renewal, so records must be producible on request, often within a short deadline such as 21 days for NSW solicitors.

blocks.text: Records design is covered in [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records) and [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).
The individual's credential decides. A person can hold several: a lawyer who is also a registered tax agent has CLE or CPD for legal practice and CPE for tax registration, each with its own rules.

items: List every credential each employee holds and the body that governs it.
Record each body's term, unit, cycle dates, mandatory subjects, caps and retention period.
Tag internal learning with the credit type, duration and subject fields those bodies need.
Give employees records they can use in their own declarations, since the obligation sits with them.
Check whether the organization itself has duties, such as an employer verifying registration or a regulated firm meeting its own competence rules.

blocks.text: Profession specific detail is on [Ahpra CPD registration standards](/regulations/ahpra-cpd-registration-standards), [US CPA CPE requirements](/regulations/us-cpa-cpe-requirements) and [US attorney CLE requirements by state](/regulations/us-attorney-cle-requirements-by-state). Firm level continuing education, such as [FINRA's Firm Element](/regulations/finra-continuing-education-requirements), is a different obligation that sits with the employer.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each credential body's rules as structured requirements and tags learning outcomes with the subject areas and durations they satisfy. Internal programs can then show which CPD, CPE or CLE requirements each activity supports, and records carry the fields auditors ask for.

faqs.q: Can one course count for CPD, CPE and CLE at the same time?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but only if each body accepts it under its own rules. Subject relevance, provider approval, unit length and verification all differ. Recalculate credit for each body, for example converting minutes into 50 minute CPE credits for US accountancy, rather than reusing one figure.

faqs.q: Is CPD a legal requirement or a professional one?
faqs.a: It depends on the profession. For Australian registered health practitioners, CPD is required by section 128 of the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law, and for Australian lawyers it is a condition of the practicing certificate. For CPA Australia members it is a membership by-law. Failure can affect registration, the right to practice or membership.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for CPD, CPE or CLE compliance, the employee or the employer?
faqs.a: Usually the individual credential holder, who declares compliance at renewal and may be audited. Employers typically provide much of the learning and may need to verify registration, so good records serve both. Some regimes, such as FINRA's Firm Element, place separate continuing education duties on the firm.

faqs.q: Do CPD hours carry over to the next cycle?
faqs.a: Rules vary. NSW solicitors may carry over up to 3 units completed between January and March, while California's accountancy board allows no carryover. Check each body's rule before relying on excess hours.
